name: CBGB (original site)
description: Legendary punk club founded by Hilly Kristal. Launch pad for the Ramones, Blondie, Patti Smith, Talking Heads, and Television. Building is a contributing property in the Bowery Historic District (added to the National Register in 2013). Now a menswear store that preserves some original interior elements.

name: Village Vanguard
description: Oldest continuously operating jazz club in NYC, opened by Max Gordon. Started as a folk and beat-poetry venue, became a jazz landmark from 1957 onward, hosting Coltrane, Miles Davis, and generations of jazz legends since.

name: Cafe Wha?
description: Folk/coffeehouse venue where Bob Dylan played some of his first NYC gigs; also an early stage for Jimi Hendrix and Bruce Springsteen.

name: Gerde's Folk City (site)
description: Central hub of the Village folk revival. Hosted Bob Dylan's first paid NYC performance, opening for John Lee Hooker in 1961.

name: The Bitter End
description: One of NYC's oldest rock clubs still operating in its original location. Early stage for Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young, and Lady Gaga decades later.

name: Electric Lady Studios
description: Recording studio built by Jimi Hendrix, one of the first artist-owned studios in the world. Still an active professional studio today.

name: Bowery Ballroom
description: Beloved mid-size indie/rock venue known for its Art Deco interior and reliably great sound.

name: Physical Graffiti cover location
address: 96–98 St Marks Place, New York, NY 10009
description: Led Zeppelin's iconic double-album cover, shot on this East Village block. Designer Peter Corriston cropped a floor out of the buildings to fit the square format. Also used by the Rolling Stones for their 'Waiting on a Friend' video.

name: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan cover location
address: Jones St & W 4th St, New York, NY 10014
description: Dylan and girlfriend Suze Rotolo walking down snowy Jones Street, one of the most reproduced album covers of all time.

name: An Innocent Man cover location
description: Billy Joel's cover shot in Soho for his doo-wop/R&B homage album.

name: Ramones debut album cover location
address: Albert's Garden, 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10003
description: Shot by Roberta Bayley against a wall in this private East Village community garden; became the definitive image of the band.

name: Joey Ramone Place
address: Bowery & E 2nd St, New York, NY 10003
description: Street co-named in honor of the Ramones' frontman, right around the corner from the old CBGB site.

name: Arturo Vega's Loft
description: Home base and rehearsal space of the Ramones' longtime art director, who designed the band's iconic eagle logo.

name: Washington Square Park
address: Washington Square Park, New York, NY 10012
description: Sunday folk gatherings here in the 1950s-60s helped ignite the Village folk scene; still a busker hub today.
